key_insight: In the Bern Sleep-Wake Registry, gpt-oss-20b extracted comorbidities with 0.88 F1 and matched the earliest reported diagnosis date to the exact day in 86.73% of cases.
clinical_relevance: Automated extraction could help build longitudinal clinical registries while reducing direct annotation costs, without establishing true disease-onset dates.
method: Analyzed 2,343 clinical entries from 248 patients across 32 diagnostic categories in six comorbidity groups.
Extracted diagnosis presence, diagnostic-instance counts, and dates using gpt-oss-20b.
Compared outputs with independent physician reviews adjudicated by a third physician.
evidence_signal: Against the adjudicated reference, cumulative date extraction achieved 87.63% recall and 58.19% full agreement; direct annotation costs were 94.65% lower.
watch_item: The 20.88% extra-date rate and evaluation within one registry warrant temporal-output review and external validation before broader use.
paper_title: Bern Sleep-Wake Registry: temporal extraction of comorbidities from unstructured clinical text using a large language model
